codeReview.summary: Solid implementation of runtime.Bounded[Req, Upd] with comprehensive test coverage. The generic bounded runtime correctly encapsulates the goroutine lifecycle pattern. ConsoleAskRuntime and ConsoleCancelRuntime were successfully refactored to delegate to Bounded with careful preservation of the ErrStopped → ctx.Err() error mapping for backward compatibility. All 7 required behaviors (i)-(vii) are covered by dedicated tests, plus 8 additional edge-case tests. All tests pass with -race, goleak.VerifyTestMain provides leak detection, and existing runtime tests are completely unchanged.

issues.description: Doc comment says 'closed exactly once after the goroutine drains' and line 135 says 'after draining any pending items'. This is slightly misleading — the run() loop does NOT drain all pending items from the request buffer on Stop(). When ctx is cancelled, run() exits immediately via the <-b.ctx.Done() branch, dropping any items still in the request channel buffer. Only the currently-processing item is completed. This is actually correct behavior (fast termination), but the doc comments over-promise. Suggest changing to 'closed exactly once after the goroutine exits' without mentioning drain.

The run() loop's second select (sending the update after handler returns) checks ctx.Done() and returns immediately if cancelled, even though the handler already completed. This means a successfully processed request's update may be dropped if Stop() races with the send. This is consistent with the 'fast termination' model and matches the old runtime behavior, but worth noting for clarity.

TestBounded_ProcessesAllEnqueuedBeforeStop uses time.Sleep(100ms) to let the handler process before calling Stop(). This is a timing-dependent test that could flake under extreme system load. However, since simpleHandler is near-instantaneous (no IO) and the buffer is 8 (ample for 4 items), this is acceptable in practice.

The ErrStopped → rt.bounded.Context().Err() mapping preserves the old behavior where Enqueue returned ctx.Err() when the runtime's context was cancelled. However, there's a subtle difference: if the *parent* context (not the Bounded internal context) was cancelled externally, the old code returned parentCtx.Err() while the new code returns bounded.ctx.Err() (which is a child context — the error will be context.Canceled in both cases for a normal cancel). This is correct because context.WithCancel propagation always results in context.Canceled, so the observable behavior is identical.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The tui-engineer-worker skill's example handoff lists ConsoleStreamPump as one of the three runtimes that should delegate to Bounded. The worker correctly identified that ConsoleStreamPump's source-driven model (SSE callback-based, no Enqueue) doesn't fit Bounded's request-driven pattern and kept it independent. The skill should clarify that source-driven runtimes are an expected exception to the delegation requirement.

summary: PASS. The implementation is well-structured and thorough. runtime.Bounded[Req, Upd] provides a clean generic abstraction with all 7 required concurrency behaviors tested (configurable buffer, idempotent Stop, ErrStopped sentinel, Updates close-once, ctx cancellation, goroutine leak-free, concurrent enqueue+stop). ConsoleAskRuntime and ConsoleCancelRuntime successfully delegate to Bounded with careful backward-compatible error mapping. ConsoleStreamPump was correctly kept independent due to its source-driven model. Four non-blocking issues found: slightly misleading doc comments about drain behavior, a timing-dependent test (acceptable in practice), and two documentation gaps in the shared state. No blocking issues.
